cases.statement: One affected person (III.3, a 5-month-old Mauritanian boy, homozygous) and his two healthy parents (each heterozygous). An affected brother (III.2) died at 8 months and was not genotyped.

people.label: III.3
people.key_phenotypes: delayed umbilical cord separation (four weeks); recurrent infections from day four of life; hyperleukocytosis (80,000/mm3); oral thrush; neutrophil CD18 expression 1.51% vs 99.9% in control

quotes.quote: Umbilical cord separation was delayed, occurring at four weeks.
The symptoms started on day four of life by the successive occurrence of several episodes of infection.
The fifth and last episode at four months consisted of fever and a persistence of hyperleukocytosis at 80,000 elements/mm^3 for which antibiotics were given but showed no improvement.
Oral thrush was found as well as hair scarcity.
showed a homozygous INDEL mutation of three nucleotides in exon 7, c.844_846delAAC (Figure 3(a)).

Parents are healthy and first-degree consanguineous, suggesting an inherited disease with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.

Parents are healthy and first-degree consanguineous, suggesting an inherited disease with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The proband had delayed cord separation, recurrent infections from the neonatal period, marked leukocytosis and severely reduced CD18 and CD11c on neutrophils by flow cytometry; the authors judge the presentation consistent with LAD1. Neutrophil oxidative burst was normal, HLA-DR expression and lymphocyte subsets were normal apart from raised NK cells. Only ITGB2 was sequenced; no other genes were tested.

quotes.quote: In the surface of neutrophils, this reduction concerns the expression of both CD18 (1.51% vs 99.9% and MFI ratio: 7.7 vs 46.2) and CD11c (0.21% vs 99.6% and MFI ratio: 3.3 vs 24.6).
Neutrophils also showed a normal oxidative burst activity.
We report a case of a five-month-old male of Mauritanian origin with clinical and biological features consistent with LAD1 disease.
We sequenced all exons and flanking intronic sequences of ITGB2 using the primers and PCR conditions of Yassaee et al. [13].

segregation.statement: Both healthy parents (first-degree consanguineous) are heterozygous. An older brother III.2 died at 8 months with recurrent infections and delayed cord fall but was not genotyped. A healthy brother III.1 (4 years) is not reported as genotyped (pedigree marks tested people with an asterisk; the text says samples came from the patient and parents).

quotes.quote: Segregation analysis showed that the two parents were heterozygous for this mutation.
Brother III.2 died at the age of eight months from septic shock with a cutaneous starting point and had a notion of recurrent infections and delayed cord fall.
The older brother III.1, aged 4 years, is healthy.
The blood samples were collected from the patient and their parents.

de_novo.statement: not applicable (homozygous, inherited from two heterozygous parents); parentage confirmation not reported.

quotes.quote: The p.Asn282del mutation was heterozygous in the child's parents, whereas it was absent in the 96 control individuals from North Africa.

in_trans.statement: Homozygous in the proband; both parents tested and heterozygous, consistent with one copy from each parent.

quotes.quote: Segregation analysis showed that the two parents were heterozygous for this mutation.

functional.statement: Patient cells (peripheral blood neutrophils and monocytes), flow cytometry against a normal control run in the same batch: reduced CD18 (1.51% vs 99.9% positive; MFI ratio 7.7 vs 46.2) and CD11c (0.21% vs 99.6%; MFI ratio 3.3 vs 24.6) on neutrophils. No construct or expression study of the variant. Molecular modeling (in silico, YASARA/Swiss Model) suggested loss of hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions of Asn282.

quotes.quote: However, the patient showed a significantly reduced expression of integrin molecules on both neutrophils and monocytes compared to the normal control tested in the same batch (Figure 2).
In the surface of neutrophils, this reduction concerns the expression of both CD18 (1.51% vs 99.9% and MFI ratio: 7.7 vs 46.2) and CD11c (0.21% vs 99.6% and MFI ratio: 3.3 vs 24.6).
Therefore, based on this in silico analysis, the loss of these interactions due to Asn282 deletion may affect the structure of integrin beta-2 and subsequently its interaction with integrin alpha-X.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: In-frame deletion of one codon (p.Asn282del, from the batch HGVS) in exon 7. The authors state LAD is caused by loss of function of CD18, that the codon lies in the domain encoded by exons 5 to 9, and that other changes at the same codon were previously described.

quotes.quote: This nonframeshift mutation results, at the protein level, in a deletion of the asparagine amino acid at position 282 (p.Asn282del).
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is a primary immune deficiency disorder with an autosomal recessive mode of inheritance, caused by loss of function of the differentiation cluster 18 (CD18) [1].

The p.Asn282del is located in a highly conserved protein domain from 124 to 364 amino acids called Von Willebrand Factor type A encoded by exons 5 to 9, where most of the known pathogenic mutations are located.
Moreover, the Asn282del is localized in the same codon where two already pathogenic variants p.Asn282Lys and Asn282ThrfsX41 were described [17].
Furthermore, it affects a highly conserved codon across multiple species (Figure 3(b)).

computational_predictions.statement: PROVEAN -12.65 (deleterious); MutationTaster 0.99 (disease causing), as reported by the authors.

quotes.quote: | ITGB2 | NM_000211.5 | Exon 7 | c.844_846delAAC | p.Asn282del | Deleterious (-12.65) | Disease causing (0.99) |
Analysis of this ITGB2 novel mutation by the in silico PROVEAN software yielded a score of -12.65, showing that it is deleterious.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Authors report absence from gnomAD exomes and genome databases, and from 96 healthy Moroccan controls sequenced for exon 7.

quotes.quote: The p.N282del mutation had not been reported previously in LAD1 disease; it is not present in gnomAD exome, in genome databases, and in 96 control individuals from Morocco, belonging to the same North African population as the studied patient.
Ninety-six DNA samples from healthy individuals all of Moroccan origin were sequenced for ITGB2 exon 7 to verify the frequency of the novel mutation identified.

authors_classification.statement: Authors call it a novel pathogenic mutation, without ACMG criteria.

quotes.quote: In summary, we report a novel pathogenic mutation p.Asn282del associated with LAD1 that expands the mutation diversity of ITGB2 and suggest the combination of flow cytometry and ITGB2 sequencing as a first-line diagnostic approach for LAD disease.
This variant was evaluated by two in silico mutation analysis tools, PROVEAN and MutationTaster, which predicted that the mutation was likely to be pathogenic.

concerns: The Figure 3 legend calls the variant a 'novel missense mutation', which contradicts the text's description as an in-frame (nonframeshift) deletion.
The Conclusions write the transcript as 'NM_ 0000211.5' (typo); Table 1 gives NM_000211.5, matching the batch.
The two parent rows (LAD1-ID0218, LAD1-ID0219) are unaffected heterozygous carriers, not affected cases; their sexes are not given separately.
The affected brother III.2 (died at 8 months, recurrent infections, delayed cord fall) was not genotyped and is not in the batch; the healthy brother III.1 is not reported as genotyped.
Functional evidence is patient-cell CD18/CD11c expression and in-silico modeling only; no variant construct was tested.
Control population described as 'North Africa' in the abstract and 'Moroccan origin' in methods; the proband is Mauritanian.
notes_for_panel: Single-family report: homozygous proband from a first-degree consanguineous Mauritanian family, both healthy parents heterozygous, Sanger sequencing of ITGB2 only. Neutrophil CD18 about 1.5% of control. Protein in the paper (p.Asn282del) agrees with the cDNA.
